confirmed_gap: The world feature reattaches when its companion key changes, but travel depends on sessions and retains its running instance. Existing current_player_view_rows() seeding only ran in the travel factory, so a current row accepted before the new world observer attached was never dispatched to that running executor.
exact_change: Move the existing factory seed into the shared seed_current_views(worker,companion) callback, retaining the original fresh authenticated resolver and current world-session filter.
After the original world observer attaches, invoke that same callback only if the existing travel slot is running and owns an instance.
Keep the original travel factory call for initial construction. No further polling, world reader, timer, protocol or ACK route is added.
row_provenance: Only companion.current_player_view_rows(), whose existing cache stores complete original v2 rows after actual reducer accepted=true/reason=applied in the current world session. Original seq, session, native binding, lifecycle player/view, position, yaw and pitch are retained. The original Server.observe_world queue and seq/view deduplication remain authoritative.
single_chain: Future accepted rows still use the original set_world_observer -> api:on_world -> composition emit(world) -> travel:observe_world chain. Cached attach rows use the exact existing factory seed path into that same travel queue; they never reenter the native reducer or chunk/material consumers.
remaining_runtime_acceptance: Sole runtime owner loads the merged source through the existing lifecycle, then verifies the existing accepted current row reaches running travel and its original prepare/replication/mapping/camera/final-ACK route. Source checks do not declare current mapping_applied or waitingACK complete.

validation.scenario: Existing initial view1 -> already-running travel -> new companion accepts original view3 before observer attach -> world reattach forwards it without rebuilding travel -> unchanged world tick does not resend -> later accepted view4 follows original observer.
